text: The midbody is an organelle formed between daughter cells during cytokinesis, required for their final separation. Midbody derivatives (MBds) persist long after division, fate unclear. MBds are inherited asymmetrically by the daughter cell with the older centrosome and selectively accumulate in stem cells, induced pluripotent stem cells, and potential cancer 'stem cells' in vivo and in vitro. MBd loss accompanies stem-cell differentiation, involving autophagic degradation via NBR1 binding to CEP55. Differentiating and normal dividing cells do not accumulate MBds and have high autophagic activity; stem and cancer cells accumulate MBds by evading autophagosome encapsulation, showing low autophagic activity. MBd enrichment enhances reprogramming to induced pluripotent stem cells and increases in vitro tumorigenicity of cancer cells, indicating unexpected roles in stem cells and cancer 'stem cells'.
